question: Why is the average velocity of free electrons in a conductor zero in the absence of an applied potential difference? Give reason.

options.A: The average velocity is zero because free electrons have no thermal motion in the absence of a potential difference.
options.B: Free electrons move randomly due to thermal agitation, and their velocities in different directions cancel on average; without an electric field there is no drift velocity.
options.C: The average velocity is zero because all electrons move with equal speed in the same direction.
options.D: The average velocity is zero because free electrons are absent in a conductor.
